title: The Starting Lineup and Unforgivable Trash Talk
paragraphs: Jesus went back to the meeting place, and there was a guy there with a crippled, shriveled hand. The religious leaders watched Jesus like hawks, waiting to see if he would heal the guy on the Sabbath so they could arrest him.

Jesus told the crippled man, "Stand up right here in the middle." Then Jesus asked the leaders, "Is it legal to do good on the Sabbath, or to do evil? To save a life, or kill?" They sat there in dead silence.
Jesus looked around at them, absolutely furious and deeply heartbroken by how stubborn and cold they were. He told the man, "Stretch out your hand." The man did, and it was perfectly healed.
The religious leaders immediately stormed out and held a secret meeting with corrupt politicians to figure out how to assassinate Jesus.

The crowds following Jesus were getting dangerously huge. People from Galilee, Judea, Jerusalem, Idumea, across the Jordan, and around Tyre and Sidon had heard the reports and came to see for themselves. He had healed so many people that everyone who had something wrong was pushing and shoving just to touch him. He had to have his disciples keep a small boat ready so he wouldn't get trampled by the crowd.
Whenever the evil spirits saw Jesus, they'd fall down right in front of him and scream, "You are the Son of God!" But Jesus shut them down hard—he warned them not to tell anyone who he was.

Jesus hiked up a mountain and called up the specific guys he wanted on his core team. He appointed twelve of them to be his official "apostles" (messengers). The plan was that they would be with him, and he would send them out to proclaim the Word and give them authority to banish demons. They were: Simon—Jesus named him Peter, meaning "Rock"; James son of Zebedee and his brother John—Jesus nicknamed the brothers Boanerges, meaning "Sons of Thunder"; Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot (who betrayed him).

Jesus went home, but the crowd was so crazy he and his guys couldn't even eat. The people closest to him heard what was going on and came to take charge of him, by force if necessary—they thought he was losing it.
The religious experts from Jerusalem showed up and started a rumor: "He's possessed by Beelzebul (Satan). He's only kicking out demons because he's getting his power from the boss of the demons."

Jesus called them over and exposed how clueless that logic was: "Does it make sense to send a devil to catch a devil—to use Satan to get rid of Satan? A constantly squabbling family disintegrates. If Satan were fighting Satan, there soon wouldn't be any Satan left. And do you think you can walk into the house of a strong, wide-awake man in broad daylight and walk off with his stuff unless you tie him up first? Tie him up, though, and you can clean him out."

Then he gave them a hardcore warning: "You can be forgiven for almost any sin or trash-talk. But if you deliberately trash-talk the Holy Spirit and call the work of God the work of the devil, that is unforgivable. You carry that guilt forever."

Then Jesus' mother and brothers showed up. They stood outside and sent someone in to tell Jesus they needed to talk. Jesus was surrounded by a crowd when he heard, "Your mother and brothers and sisters are outside looking for you."

Jesus answered, "Who do you think my mother and brothers are?" Then he looked around at everyone sitting in a circle and said, "My mother and brothers are right here in front of you. Obedience runs thicker than blood. Anyone who lives by God's will—that's my brother, my sister, my mother."
